# WhatsApp Gateway

> A Go-based REST API gateway that abstracts WhatsApp Web complexity for stateless backend integration.

## What this does

This gateway handles all WhatsApp connection state, session management, and message handling. Your backend stays stateless and only needs to make HTTP calls and handle webhooks.

Key capabilities:
- Send and receive WhatsApp messages via REST API
- Multi-device support (one gateway instance handles multiple WhatsApp accounts)
- QR code and pairing code login methods
- Webhook-based incoming message notifications
- Message reactions, editing, and deletion

## Who this is for

Backend developers who want to:
- Integrate WhatsApp messaging without managing WhatsApp sessions
- Keep their backend stateless and horizontally scalable
- Use any programming language (language-agnostic HTTP API)

## Base URL

All API endpoints are prefixed with `/api/v1`.

Example: `http://localhost:3000/api/v1/message/text`

## Authentication

The gateway uses JWT tokens scoped to phone numbers.

### Step 1: Register and get JWT

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v1/register \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "phone_number": "6281234567890",
    "secret_key": "your_basic_auth_secret"
  }'
```

Response:
```json
{
  "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
}
```

### Step 2: Use JWT in all subsequent requests

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v1/message/text \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"chat": "6289876543210", "message": "Hello!"}'
```

> **Recipient addressing:** every message/contact endpoint takes `chat` (canonical) or the
> deprecated `msisdn` alias; `chat` wins when both are set. `chat` accepts a bare phone number,
> a user JID (`@s.whatsapp.net`), a group JID (`@g.us`) — so you can message groups — or a `@lid`
> (best-effort; not guaranteed dialable). Send responses echo the resolved canonical `chat`.

> **Group/community ops require an explicit `@g.us`** — a group op never lands on a user JID (a bare
> number or user JID is a 400). Batch mutations (add/remove/promote/demote, approve/reject) return
> **200 partial success** with per-participant `results[]`, never an overall error for one bad member.
> Ban-safety gates (default): the whole mutation surface is behind `GROUP_MANAGEMENT_ENABLED` (404 when
> off); **bulk participant add** and **join-via-link (mass join)** are gated OFF (`GROUP_ADD_PARTICIPANTS_ENABLED`,
> `GROUP_JOIN_VIA_LINK_ENABLED`) and return 403 until enabled.

> **Replies & mentions (all sends):** every `POST /message/*` send (text, image, audio, video, document,
> location, poll, sticker) accepts `reply_to_id` + `reply_to_sender` (+ optional `reply_to_text` for the
> quoted preview) to quote a message, and `mentions[]` (numbers/JIDs) to @-tag. Storeless (caller supplies
> the quoted context). Works in direct and queue modes. On multipart endpoints (image/audio/video/document/
> sticker) send `mentions` as repeated form fields, not comma-joined. A mention renders inline only where a
> caption/text carries the matching `@<number>`; sticker/location/poll still fire the mention notification.

> **Idempotent sends:** send an `Idempotency-Key` header on any `POST /message/*` to make retries
> safe. A repeat of the same key replays the original response (`Idempotent-Replay: true`) instead
> of sending twice; an in-flight duplicate gets `409`; the same key with a different body gets `422`.
> DB-backed (keyed by JWT account + key), survives restarts. Queue mode is enqueued-once, not
> delivered-once. Tune via `IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_SECONDS` / `IDEMPOTENCY_PENDING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`.

### Step 3: Login to WhatsApp

Use either QR code or pairing code:

**QR Code (JSON format):**
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v1/login/qr_code/json \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN"
```

**Pairing Code:**
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v1/login/pair_code \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN"
```

### Step 4: Check connection status

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/api/v1/login/status \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN"
```

## Security Warnings

### CRITICAL: Gateway Must Be Wrapped by Your Backend

**DO NOT expose this gateway directly to end users.** Always place it behind your backend service that:
- Authenticates users
- Verifies phone number ownership
- Prevents unauthorized registrations
- Implements rate limiting
- Enforces business rules

### JWT Token Sharing Issue

If two JWT tokens are generated for the same phone number, **both can access the WhatsApp session** once either logs in.

Example vulnerability:
1. User A registers phone "123" -> Token 1
2. User B registers same phone "123" -> Token 2
3. User A logs into WhatsApp
4. **User B can now access the session with Token 2**

**Mitigation**: Your backend must prevent duplicate registrations and verify phone number ownership.

### Production Requirements

- Use PostgreSQL with SSL (not SQLite)
- Strong secrets (32+ characters, cryptographically random)
- Disable interactive documentation (`ENABLE_DOCUMENTATION=false`)
- HTTPS via reverse proxy
- Deploy in private network/VPC
- Verify webhook HMAC signatures

## Integration Patterns

### Pattern 1: User Registration Flow

```javascript
// Your backend handles user authentication
app.post('/connect-whatsapp', authenticateUser, async (req, res) => {
  // Call gateway to get JWT for this user's phone
  const response = await fetch('http://gateway:3000/api/v1/register', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      phone_number: req.user.phone,
      secret_key: process.env.GATEWAY_SECRET
    })
  });

  const { token } = await response.json();

  // Store token securely associated with user
  // Return QR code endpoint to frontend
  res.json({
    qr_url: `http://gateway:3000/api/v1/login/qr_code/html`,
    token: token // Or keep server-side and proxy requests
  });
});
```

### Pattern 2: Sending Messages

```python
import requests

def send_whatsapp_message(user_phone, recipient, message):
    # Get stored JWT for this user
    jwt_token = get_user_jwt(user_phone)

    response = requests.post(
        'http://gateway:3000/api/v1/message/text',
        headers={
            'Authorization': f'Bearer {jwt_token}',
            'Content-Type': 'application/json'
        },
        json={
            'msisdn': recipient,
            'message': message
        }
    )

    return response.json()
```

### Pattern 3: Handling Webhooks

```javascript
app.post('/webhook', (req, res) => {
  // Verify HMAC signature (recommended)
  const signature = req.headers['x-webhook-signature'];
  if (!verifyHmac(req.body, signature)) {
    return res.status(401).send('Invalid signature');
  }

  const { event, phone_number, message_id, to, text } = req.body;

  switch (event) {
    case 'message.sent':
      console.log(`Message ${message_id} sent to ${to}`);
      break;
    case 'message.failed':
      console.log(`Message ${message_id} failed`);
      break;
    case 'message.incoming':
      console.log(`Incoming message from ${req.body.from}: ${text}`);
      break;
  }

  res.json({ success: true });
});
```

## Webhook Events

The gateway sends webhooks to your registered URL for message events.

Event types:
- `message.queued` - Message queued for sending
- `message.sent` - Message successfully sent
- `message.failed` - Message failed to send
- `message.incoming` - Incoming message received

Incoming-message webhooks include an `addressing_mode` field:
- `"pn"` - `from` is a callable `@s.whatsapp.net` phone number
- `"lid"` - the sender could only be resolved to an opaque `@lid` (e.g. a group LID-only participant); do not treat `from` as dialable

## Recipient Address Format

- **Individual chat**: `{phone}@s.whatsapp.net` (e.g., `6281234567890@s.whatsapp.net`)
- **Group chat**: `{group_id}@g.us` (e.g., `120363xxxxx@g.us`)

## API Reference

For complete API documentation, including all endpoints, request/response schemas, field types, and validation rules, refer to the OpenAPI specification:

**Public URL:** https://waga.glennprays.com/openapi.yaml

**From running gateway:** `GET /docs/openapi.yaml` (if documentation is enabled)

**From GitHub:** https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glennprays/whatsapp-gateway/main/docs/openapi.yaml

### Quick Reference

| Category | Endpoints |
|----------|-----------|
| Auth | `POST /register`, `POST /login/qr_code/{format}`, `POST /login/pair_code`, `GET /login/status`, `POST /logout`, `POST /session/reconnect` |
| Webhooks | `GET /webhook`, `POST /webhook`, `DELETE /webhook` |
| Messaging | `POST /message/text`, `POST /message/image`, `POST /message/audio` (is_ptt = voice note), `POST /message/video` (caption/is_gif), `POST /message/document` (file_name/caption), `POST /message/location`, `POST /message/poll`, `POST /message/sticker`, `POST /message/react`, `PUT /message` (edit), `DELETE /message` |
| Interaction | `POST /message/read` (blue ticks; `message_ids[]`, `sender` required for groups), `POST /chat/presence` (typing indicator; `state`=composing/recording/paused) — both counted against the interim action cap |
| Contact | `GET /contact/check?chat=` (IsOnWhatsApp validation; returns jid/is_on_whatsapp/verified_name), `GET /contact/` (list synced contacts; paginated limit/offset; local store, never 404 on empty), `GET /contact/info?chat=` (server profile: status/picture_id/verified_name/device_count; cached+budgeted), `GET /contact/avatar?chat=&preview=` (avatar URL+id for a user OR group; ETag via If-None-Match → 304; 404 none / 403 hidden) |
| Group (reads) | `GET /group/` (list joined groups; server read, short-TTL cached + per-account read budget, 429 when exhausted), `GET /group/info?chat=<@g.us>` (one group's full detail + participant roster; 403 if not a member, 404 if absent) |
| Group (mutations) | `POST /group/` (create group/community; add-on-create gated), `POST /group/leave`, `POST /group/participants` (`action`=add/remove/promote/demote; add gated; **200 partial success** with `results[]` — privacy-blocked add → invited, non-member promote → failed; self in remove/promote/demote → 400, use leave), `PATCH /group/settings` (announce/locked), `PATCH /group/name` (≤25), `PATCH /group/topic` (≤512), `PUT /group/photo` (multipart JPEG), `DELETE /group/photo`, `GET /group/invite` + `POST /group/invite/reset` (admin invite link), `GET /group/invite/info?code=` (preview, no join; 410 if revoked), `POST /group/join` (**mass-join, gated → 403**), `GET /group/requests` + `POST /group/requests` (list / approve-reject join requests; approve/reject is 200 partial success) — all gated by `GROUP_MANAGEMENT_ENABLED` (404 when off) |
| Community (reads) | `GET /community/subgroups?chat=<@g.us>` (list linked sub-groups; empty list if none, not an error), `GET /community/participants?chat=<@g.us>` (all participants across linked groups; primary JID only) — server reads, cached + budgeted; a non-community group returns 400/403/404 |
| Community (mutations) | `POST /community/subgroups` (link a sub-group under a parent community; body `{chat, child_jid}`), `DELETE /community/subgroups?chat=&child=` (unlink) — gated by `GROUP_MANAGEMENT_ENABLED` (404 when off) |
| Health | `GET /health`, `GET /health/live`, `GET /health/ready` |
| Admin (ROOT path, operator-only) | `GET /admin/sessions` (per-instance session inventory: honest `connected`/`disconnected`/`never_paired`/`logged_out`/`banned` states merged from live clients + device store + persisted status; masked phones + `instance` hostname), `GET /admin/sessions/{phone}` (one account or 404) |
| Metrics (ROOT path, operator-only) | `GET /metrics` (hand-rolled Prometheus text; `whatsapp_gateway_messages_total`, `whatsapp_gateway_webhook_deliveries_total`, `whatsapp_gateway_sessions{state}`) |

**Admin / metrics plane** live at the **ROOT path** (not under the `/api/v1` base) and are **operator-only, cross-tenant**. They are **dark by default**: with no `ADMIN_API_SECRET` the routes are unregistered and return `404`; when set, send `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` (constant-time). `/metrics` additionally needs `METRICS_ENABLED=true`. Never labelled by phone number (cardinality); the inventory is **per-instance** (scrape each node behind a load balancer).

Direct-mode status webhooks (`message.sent`/`message.failed`/`message.queued`) are delivered **asynchronously with bounded retry** (`WEBHOOK_MAX_RETRIES`, `WEBHOOK_RETRY_BACKOFF_SECONDS`); best-effort — durable delivery requires RabbitMQ.

## Error Responses

All errors follow this format:
```json
{
  "error": "Invalid request syntax or parameters.",
  "code": 400
}
```

Common status codes: `400` (Bad Request), `401` (Unauthorized), `403` (Forbidden), `404` (Not Found), `409` (Conflict), `500` (Internal Server Error)

## Request Tracing

Include `X-Trace-ID` header with a UUID for request tracking:
```bash
curl -H "X-Trace-ID: 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" \
     http://localhost:3000/api/v1/login/status
```

## Environment Variables

Full reference mirroring `config/config.go`. Defaults come from struct tag defaults; required keys in **bold**.

### Server

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `ENV` | `development` | `development` or `production` |
| `PORT` | `3000` | HTTP listen port |
| `BASE_PATH` | `/` | URL prefix for all routes |
| `HTTP_ORIGIN` | `*` | CORS allowed origin |

### Documentation

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `ENABLE_DOCUMENTATION` | `false` | Serve interactive API docs |
| `DOCUMENTATION_USER` | `user` | Basic auth user for docs |
| `DOCUMENTATION_PASSWORD` | `password` | Basic auth password for docs |
| `DOCUMENTATION_BASE_PATH` | `/docs` | Where docs are mounted |

### Auth

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| **`JWT_SECRET`** | `secret` | JWT signing key — must be strong in prod |
| `JWT_TOKEN_DURATION_MINUTES` | `1440` | JWT lifetime; clamped to 1..525600 (24h..1y), out-of-range resets to 1440 |
| `JWT_ISSUER` | `whatsapp-gateway` | `iss` claim |
| **`SECRET_KEY`** | `secret` | Basic-auth secret for `POST /api/register` |

### WhatsApp storage

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `WHATSAPP_DATASTORE_TYPE` | `sqlite` | `sqlite` (dev) or `postgres` (prod) |
| `WHATSAPP_DATASTORE_URI` | `file:dbs/whatsapp.db?_pragma=foreign_keys(1)` | DSN |
| `WHATSAPP_DEVICE_LABEL` | `WhatsApp Gateway` | Device name shown to WhatsApp |
| **`WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_HMAC_ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY`** | `0123…cdef` (insecure default) | 32 hex chars; encrypts per-webhook HMAC secrets at rest |
| `WHATSMEOW_LOG_LEVEL` | `warn` | Verbosity of the whatsmeow client logger |

### Logging

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `LOG_LEVEL` | `info` | `debug`/`info`/`warn`/`error` |
| `LOG_OUTPUT` | `stdout` | `stdout` or `file` |
| `LOG_FILE_PATH` | `/var/log/whatsapp-gateway.log` | Used when `LOG_OUTPUT=file` |
| `LOG_ENABLE_CALLER` | `false` | Include caller file:line in each log |

### Rate limiting

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `REGISTER_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED` | `true` | Toggle per-IP throttle on `POST /register` (in-process memory limiter) |
| `REGISTER_RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS` | `5` | Max registrations per IP per window |
| `REGISTER_RATE_LIMIT_DURATION_SECONDS` | `60` | Register throttle window |
| `MESSAGE_RATE_LIMIT_PROVIDER` | `memory` | `memory`, `redis`, or `noop` |
| `MESSAGE_RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS` | `100` | Requests per window |
| `MESSAGE_RATE_LIMIT_DURATION_SECONDS` | `60` | Window length |

### Uploads

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` | `16777216` (16 MiB) | Max outbound media size (image/audio/video/document/sticker), checked before reading into memory; image/sticker/audio/video also enforce a per-kind MIME allow-list |

### RabbitMQ (optional queue mode)

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `RABBITMQ_ENABLED` | `false` | When `false`, runs in direct mode |
| `RABBITMQ_URL` | `amqp://user:user@localhost:5672/` | AMQP connection URI |
| `RABBITMQ_CONNECTION_NAME` | `whatsapp-gateway` | Connection identifier |
| `RABBITMQ_PREFETCH_COUNT` | `5` | Per-consumer prefetch |

### Redis (rate-limit backend)

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `REDIS_ENABLED` | `false` | Enables Redis-backed providers |
| `REDIS_URI` | `redis://localhost:6379/0` | Connection URI |

### Worker pools

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `WORKER_INCOMING_EVENTS` | `5` | Consumers for incoming-event queue |
| `WORKER_WEBHOOK_DELIVERY` | `10` | Consumers for webhook-delivery queue |
| `WORKER_OUTGOING_MESSAGES` | `3` | Consumers for outgoing-message queue |
| `QUEUE_MAX_RETRIES` | `3` | Retry budget per job |

### Status webhooks

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `WEBHOOK_STATUS_EVENTS_ENABLED` | `true` | Emit message lifecycle webhooks |
| `WEBHOOK_STATUS_EVENTS` | `message.sent,message.failed` | Comma-separated subset: `message.queued`, `message.sent`, `message.failed` |
| `WEBHOOK_MAX_RETRIES` | `3` | Direct-mode async webhook retry attempts (queue mode uses RabbitMQ retry) |
| `WEBHOOK_RETRY_BACKOFF_SECONDS` | `2` | Base for the exponential retry backoff |

### Admin / metrics plane (operator-only, ROOT path)

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `ADMIN_API_SECRET` | _(empty)_ | Bearer secret for `/admin/*` + `/metrics`. Empty ⇒ plane unregistered (404, dark by default); set ⇒ `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`, constant-time |
| `METRICS_ENABLED` | `false` | Expose `GET /metrics`; still needs `ADMIN_API_SECRET` set to be reachable |

### Object storage

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `STORAGE_PROVIDER` | `local` | `local` or `s3` |
| `STORAGE_S3_ENDPOINT` | `s3.amazonaws.com` | S3 API endpoint |
| `STORAGE_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | _(empty)_ | S3 access key |
| `STORAGE_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | _(empty)_ | S3 secret key |
| `STORAGE_S3_REGION` | `us-east-1` | S3 region |
| `STORAGE_S3_BUCKET` | `whatsapp-gateway` | Target bucket |
| `STORAGE_S3_USE_SSL` | `true` | TLS to S3 endpoint |
| `STORAGE_S3_PRESIGNED_URL_EXPIRY_SECONDS` | `86400` | Presigned URL TTL |
| `STORAGE_LOCAL_PATH` | `./storage` | Local-mode root |
| `STORAGE_BASE_URL` | _(empty)_ | Public base URL for stored objects |
| `STORAGE_API_PATH` | `/storage` | Mount path when serving local storage |

### Webhook media download

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `WEBHOOK_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD_ENABLED` | `false` | Download incoming media and re-host |
| `WEBHOOK_MEDIA_STORAGE_PREFIX` | `webhook/media` | Storage key prefix |
| `WEBHOOK_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `30` | Per-file download timeout |
| `WEBHOOK_MEDIA_FALLBACK_TO_WHATSAPP_URL` | `true` | If download fails, send raw WhatsApp URL |
| `WEBHOOK_MEDIA_RETENTION_DAYS` | `30` | Days before lifecycle deletion |
| `WEBHOOK_MEDIA_MAX_FILE_SIZE_BYTES` | `10485760` | 10 MiB cap |

### Storage lifecycle

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `STORAGE_AUTO_DELETE_ENABLED` | `false` | Run periodic retention sweep |
| `STORAGE_AUTO_DELETE_INTERVAL_HOURS` | `24` | Sweep cadence |

Canonical reference: [environment-variables.md](https://waga.glennprays.com/assets/docs/environment-variables.md).

## MCP (Model Context Protocol)

A standalone MCP server bridges AI agents — Claude, Cursor, Claude Code, and other MCP-capable clients — to this gateway. The agent invokes MCP tools (send text/image, edit/delete/react to messages, manage webhooks, check connection status); the MCP server translates each tool call into an authenticated HTTP request against the gateway using a pre-issued JWT scoped to one phone number.

```
AI Agent  <--MCP (stdio or HTTP+SSE)-->  MCP WhatsApp Gateway  <--HTTP/JWT-->  WhatsApp Gateway (this service)
```

The MCP server is a separate component from the gateway itself — you deploy the gateway, mint a JWT via `POST /api/register`, then configure the MCP server with that token. The gateway handles all WhatsApp protocol logic; the MCP server only exposes the tool surface to the agent.

| Doc | Link |
|-----|------|
| Introduction | https://waga.glennprays.com/assets/docs/mcp/introduction.md |
| Quick Start | https://waga.glennprays.com/assets/docs/mcp/quick-start.md |

## Tech Stack

- Go 1.25
- whatsmeow (WhatsApp Web protocol library)
- Fiber (HTTP framework)
- SQLite / PostgreSQL
- JWT authentication
- Google Wire (dependency injection)
